OVERVIEW

Create an AWS architecture diagram for ServiceGremlin, a graph-based infrastructure dependency visualizer.

The diagram contains:
- Users (client outside AWS Cloud)
- AWS Cloud (outermost container enclosing all AWS resources)
- Web UI component (logical group)
- Client API (logical group)
- Storage management component (logical group)
- Cost component (logical group)
- VPC (AWS infrastructure container)
- Private subnet (AWS infrastructure container inside VPC)
- Data component (logical group inside Private subnet)
- Discovery component (logical group inside Private subnet)
- Image deployment component (logical group)

Arrange the top-level layout from left to right in this order:
Users -> Web UI component -> Client API -> Storage management & Cost -> VPC (Data + Discovery) -> Image deployment component

LOGICAL STRUCTURE & GROUPS

AWS Cloud contains all AWS services and groups.
Users stay outside AWS Cloud.

WEB UI COMPONENT

Create a dashed logical group called "Web UI component".
It contains:
- Web UI

Users access Web UI.

CLIENT API

Create a dashed logical group called "Client API".
It contains:
- AWS WAF
- AWS AppSync
- Amazon API Gateway, label: "ServiceGremlin API"
- Amazon CloudWatch
- AWS Systems Manager

Arrange them vertically.

Web UI -> AWS WAF
AWS WAF -> AWS AppSync
AWS AppSync -> Amazon CloudWatch
AWS AppSync -> AWS Systems Manager
Amazon API Gateway ServiceGremlin API -> Amazon CloudWatch
Amazon API Gateway ServiceGremlin API -> AWS Systems Manager

COST COMPONENT

Create a dashed logical group called "Cost component".
It contains:
- AWS Lambda, label: "Cost function"

STORAGE MANAGEMENT COMPONENT

Create a dashed logical group called "Storage management component".
It contains:
- Amazon Athena
- Amazon S3 bucket, label: "CURBucket"
- AWS Cost & Usage Report (CUR)
- Amazon S3 bucket, label: "AthenaResultsBucket"

Arrange them primarily left-to-right.

AWS Lambda Cost function -> Amazon Athena
Amazon Athena -> Amazon S3 CURBucket
AWS Cost & Usage Report (CUR) -> Amazon S3 CURBucket
AWS Lambda Cost function -> Amazon S3 AthenaResultsBucket

VPC & SUBNET

Create one VPC container.
Inside the VPC create one Private subnet.

Inside the Private subnet create two logical groups:
1. Data component
2. Discovery component

DATA COMPONENT

Create a dashed logical group called "Data component" inside the Private subnet.
It contains:
- AWS Lambda, label: "Gremlin function"
- Amazon Neptune
- AWS Lambda, label: "Search function"
- Amazon OpenSearch Service

Arrange Gremlin Lambda and Neptune on the upper row.
Arrange Search Lambda and OpenSearch below them.

AWS Lambda Gremlin function -> Amazon Neptune
AWS Lambda Search function -> Amazon OpenSearch Service

AWS AppSync -> AWS Lambda Gremlin function
Amazon API Gateway ServiceGremlin API -> AWS Lambda Search function

DISCOVERY COMPONENT

Create a dashed logical group called "Discovery component" inside the Private subnet.
It contains:
- Amazon Elastic Container Service
- AWS Fargate
- Amazon Elastic Container Registry

Arrange Amazon ECS above AWS Fargate and Amazon ECR.

Amazon ECS -> AWS Fargate
Amazon ECS -> Amazon ECR

DISCOVERY INPUTS

Outside the VPC but still inside AWS Cloud, place:
- Amazon API Gateway, label: "ServiceGremlin API"
- AWS SDK
- AWS Config

AWS Fargate -> AWS SDK
AWS Fargate -> AWS Config
AWS Fargate -> Amazon API Gateway ServiceGremlin API
Amazon API Gateway ServiceGremlin API -> AWS Lambda Search function

IMAGE DEPLOYMENT COMPONENT

Create a dashed logical group called "Image deployment component".
Place it on the far right.
It contains vertically, from top to bottom:
- Amazon S3 bucket, label: "DiscoveryBucket"
- AWS CodePipeline
- AWS CodeBuild
- Container image

AWS CodePipeline -> Amazon S3 DiscoveryBucket
AWS CodePipeline -> AWS CodeBuild
AWS CodeBuild -> Container image
Container image -> Amazon Elastic Container Registry

VISUAL REQUIREMENTS

AWS Cloud:
- outermost boundary
- all AWS services and groups are inside it
- Users remain outside

VPC:
- inside AWS Cloud

Private subnet:
- inside VPC

Data component and Discovery component:
- inside Private subnet

Use compact AWS icon + label nodes.
Logical component groups should use subtle dashed boundaries.
AWS infrastructure groups must use the official AWS group visual grammar.
Do not render large card-style nodes.
